$comment: packing-list screenshot traversal, copy-free. Generates qa/flows/mobile.yaml (run scripts/qa/compile-flow.mjs). Screenshot names match qa/screenshots.config.json sources (list, packers, types). Mirrors the proven hand-written flow, but deterministic: the seeded trip already carries packers, so no live add-packer typing (RN <Modal> content isn't in the iOS a11y tree anyway). The share waypoints (Tier-2 outcome coverage for the 1.0.4 shared-trip flow) ride LAST, so the share identity minted when the Share screen mounts can't disturb earlier waypoints — mirrors grocery-list's share leg. The share buttons are asserted, never tapped: Send opens the OS share sheet and Scan requests camera permission, both flaky to drive cross-platform. A screenshot immediately followed by a tap needs a settle step between them: on iOS 26 the first tap after Maestro's screenshot is swallowed (the app window has to re-take focus), which read as a dead Back button (2026-07-27).

upgrade.$comment: T5 upgrade harness — cross-version subflow (compiles to qa/flows/upgrade-write.yaml + upgrade-assert.yaml; run by scripts/qa/upgrade-test.mjs against qa/released/<platform>, full profile + nightly, NOT per-PR). The bug class: install a HEAD build over months-old data and silently lose it. 'write' runs on the LAST-RELEASED binary (QA seed + add an item named Legacy Ferry Ticket, a name absent from every itemRules list so it can only come from this write); the harness then installs HEAD OVER it (never uninstall) and runs 'assert', which proves BOTH seeded data (the Greece trip and its packer Sam) AND the written item survived. If HEAD reads the persisted trip store differently than the released build wrote it, Legacy Ferry Ticket is gone and the assert fails. Neither flow may clear state — persistence across the install is the whole point (upgradeJourneys forces clearState:false). The add rides the sticky add-item TextInput + return key, the same mutating action the T4 survival flow uses, because it is the one write that auto-saves to disk with no extra confirm step.

survival.$comment: T4 chaos net — state-survival subflow (compiles to qa/flows/state-survival.yaml; full profile + nightly, NOT per-PR). Core mutating action = add a packing item to the seeded trip (it auto-saves to disk). Then REAL process death (killApp on Android / stopApp on iOS), then relaunch keeping state and re-open the trip. Intent oracle: the item added before the kill is still on the list after it. The leading assertNot proves 'Compass' wasn't already there.
